eqourse-c-01.reviewNote: Checked against the allowed ranges of n, l, m_l and m_s; stored key C agrees.
hints: Start with the allowed orbital quantum numbers for a given principal quantum number n.
The orbital quantum number l must be an integer from 0 to n - 1. For n = 3, compare each option with that range.
eqourse-c-01.takeaway: Check the quantum-number ranges in order. A tuple is forbidden as soon as one value breaks its allowed range, even if the remaining values look valid.

pcm-c-03.reviewNote: Independently checked Q/F = 0.040 mol electrons; Ni2+ requires two electrons; theoretical mass 1.18 g; efficiency 80%.
hints: First calculate the mass of nickel that the charge would deposit if every electron contributed to nickel plating.
Each Ni2+ ion needs two electrons. Use theoretical mass = Q x M / (2F), then compare actual mass with theoretical mass.
pcm-c-03.takeaway: Current efficiency compares the actual deposited mass with the theoretical mass from Faraday's law. Account for the two electrons needed by each Ni2+ ion before calculating the percentage.
